source: Tier lists from YouTube (Jeff Nippard, Jeremy Ethier, Mike Israetel / Milo Wolf), plus a few Setsmith estimates, mapped to Hevy's exercises. Built from data/exercise-rankings.source.md and data/exercise-rankings.mapping.json by npm run build:rankings.

cues.setup: Set the seat height so the handles align with your mid-to-lower chest level. Adjust the starting position to allow a deep stretch at the bottom without putting uncomfortable stress on the shoulder joint.
cues.execution: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and depressed against the backrest throughout the set. Drive through the handles while focusing on squeezing the pecs together. Advantage: Allows safe, highly stable pushing to failure without needing a spotter.

cues.setup: Perform seated with a backrest to eliminate balancing and maximize torso stability. Set the pulleys around shoulder or upper-chest height.
cues.execution: Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout the movement. On the eccentric phase, let the cables stretch your pecs back as far as comfortable. On the concentric phase, focus on bringing your upper arms/biceps together across your chest rather than just touching your hands.

cues.setup: Set the bench flat or at a low incline (~15–30 degrees).
cues.execution: Lower the dumbbells deep past your ribcage to get a full PEC stretch (a key advantage over barbells). Keep your elbows tucked at roughly 45–60 degrees relative to your torso to protect the shoulders.

cues.setup: Set the bench flat or at a low incline (~15–30 degrees).
cues.execution: Lower the dumbbells deep past your ribcage to get a full PEC stretch (a key advantage over barbells). Keep your elbows tucked at roughly 45–60 degrees relative to your torso to protect the shoulders.

cues.setup: Lean slightly forward to bias the chest rather than staying completely upright.
cues.execution: Lower your body under control until you achieve a deep stretch in the pecs at the bottom. Press up smoothly through your palms. Use a dip belt to progressively overload as strength increases.

cues.setup: Place hands on yoga blocks, handles, or weight plates to elevate your hands above the floor.
cues.execution: Lower your chest past the level of your hands to overcome the depth limitation of standard floor push-ups and get a full PEC stretch. Pause for 2–3 seconds in the bottom stretched position for maximum stimulus.

Focus exclusively on the bottom half of the range of motion where the PEC is under high stretch and mechanical tension. Avoid bringing the dumbbells all the way to the top where tension drops to zero.
Flare your elbows out wide and lower dumbbells towards the upper chest/neck area to maximize PEC stretch. Start light to assess shoulder tolerance. (Safer alternative to the barbell version).

rankings.name: Plate Press
rankings.note: F-Tier Hell

rankings.name: Barbell Guillotine Press
rankings.note: Safety Hazard

cues.setup: Set up on a chest-supported row machine or brace your chest firmly against an incline bench (e.g., Helms Row).
cues.execution: Eliminates momentum and lower back fatigue. Drive your elbows back past your torso to hit both the lats and upper/mid back with maximum stability. Focus on pulling through the elbows rather than yanking with the hands.

cues.setup: Sit down and secure your thighs firmly under the pads to ensure stability.
cues.execution: Lean back slightly (10–15 degrees). Pull the bar down toward your upper chest, focusing on pulling your elbows down into your sides. Neutral grip offers slightly higher lat bias, while wide grip engages mid-traps and upper back alongside the lats.

cues.setup: Sit down and secure your thighs firmly under the pads to ensure stability.
cues.execution: Lean back slightly (10–15 degrees). Pull the bar down toward your upper chest, focusing on pulling your elbows down into your sides. Neutral grip offers slightly higher lat bias, while wide grip engages mid-traps and upper back alongside the lats.

cues.setup: Kneel on one knee facing a single cable stack. Brace against your front knee or an incline bench for stability.
cues.execution: Pull the cable unilaterally, driving the elbow straight down into your hip. Great for isolating each lat independently and fixing side-to-side muscular imbalances.

cues.setup: Set up at a landmine station or barbell corner, standing perpendicular to the bar. Stagger your stance and brace your opposite arm firmly against your front thigh/knee.
cues.execution: Grip the fat end of the barbell sleeve. Drive your elbow up and out to smash the upper/mid-back and traps with high tension and a deep bottom stretch.

cues.setup: Sit tall on the cable row bench with feet planted firmly.
cues.execution: Lean forward at the hips during the eccentric phase to achieve a deep stretch in the lats. Pull your elbows back to your sides, driving thoracic extension as you complete the concentric contraction.

cues.setup: Stand on bumper plates or a low platform over the barbell. Bend over until your torso is parallel to the floor.
cues.execution: The deficit allows a deeper stretch off the floor. Explosively pull the bar to your lower sternum/upper abdomen, then lower under control to a complete dead stop.

cues.setup: Use a rope or straight bar on a high pulley. Step back and hinge forward at the hips.
cues.execution: Keep a slight fixed bend in your elbows. Sweep your hands downward in an arc towards your thighs by driving strictly with your elbows. Incline your torso forward at the top to maximize the overhead lat stretch.

rankings.name: Renegade Rows
rankings.note: F-Tier Hell

rankings.name: Above-the-Knee Rack Pull
rankings.note: Equipment Hazard / Ego Lifting

cues.setup: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides or a barbell across your back. Take long strides forward.
cues.execution: Lean your torso slightly forward (~30 degrees) as you descend into each lunge to stretch the glutes deeply. Drive up and forward through your front heel/hips rather than pushing solely with your quads.

rankings.name: Machine Hip Abduction
rankings.note: Upper Glute #1 Choice

cues.setup: Sit on the machine and add a foam pad inside the leg pads if extra range of motion is desired.
cues.execution: Lean your torso forward about 30 degrees to align the resistance with upper glute (glute medius/minimus) fibers. Press outward under control and control the eccentric return for a deep stretch. High reps (15–20) or heavier loads work well.

cues.setup: Elevate your front foot on a small platform or box (2–4 inches).
cues.execution: The deficit provides extra depth and stretch at the bottom of the movement. Keep a slight forward torso lean (~30 degrees) and drive through the hip.

cues.setup: Set the pad height just below your hip crease to allow full hip flexion.
cues.execution: Round your upper back slightly (thoracic flexion) and turn your toes slightly outward to reduce spinal erector engagement and isolate the glutes. Extend at the hips to pull yourself up, squeezing the glutes hard at top lockout.

rankings.name: Machine Hip Thrust / Glute Drive
rankings.note: Mid Glute #1 Choice

cues.setup: Strap the belt comfortably across your hips below the iliac spine.
cues.execution: Superior to barbell hip thrusts due to setup ease, comfort, and stability. Drive hips straight up, locking out at the top while keeping chin tucked and ribs down to maximize mid-glute tension.

rankings.name: Romanian Deadlift
rankings.note: Lower Glute #1 Choice

cues.setup: Hold a barbell or dumbbells with a shoulder-width stance.
cues.execution: Push your hips back as far as possible (hip hinge) with a slight knee bend until you feel a deep stretch in your lower glutes and hamstrings. Drive your hips forward to lockout.

cues.setup: For split squats, place front foot far enough forward to allow a deep hip stretch. For step-ups, set box height at or slightly above knee level and hold a handle/rack for stability.
cues.execution: Lean torso forward slightly and focus on driving through the lead hip rather than extending purely through the front knee.

cues.setup: For split squats, place front foot far enough forward to allow a deep hip stretch. For step-ups, set box height at or slightly above knee level and hold a handle/rack for stability.
cues.execution: Lean torso forward slightly and focus on driving through the lead hip rather than extending purely through the front knee.

rankings.name: Donkey Kicks
rankings.note: F-Tier Hell / Worst of the Worst

cues.setup: Set the cable pulley around hand/waist height. Face away from the cable stack, take 1–2 steps forward so your arms are positioned behind your torso, placing the long head of the bicep into a maximum pre-stretch.
cues.execution: Curl both arms simultaneously while keeping your elbows set back behind your body. Drive through your pinkies to emphasize supination. Excellent movement for building the biceps peak.

cues.setup: Adjust the preacher bench to a standard ~45-degree angle. Ensure your armpits sit comfortably against the top pad with upper arms fully flush.
cues.execution: Lower the weight all the way down to full elbow extension to capitalize on high tension in the stretched position. Lock elbows in place to prevent momentum or shoulder involvement.

cues.setup: Adjust the preacher bench to a standard ~45-degree angle. Ensure your armpits sit comfortably against the top pad with upper arms fully flush.
cues.execution: Lower the weight all the way down to full elbow extension to capitalize on high tension in the stretched position. Lock elbows in place to prevent momentum or shoulder involvement.

cues.setup: Position upper arms on a 45-degree preacher bench holding dumbbells with a neutral (palms facing inward, thumbs pointing up) grip.
cues.execution: Lower under control to a complete stretch. Taking away supination shifts high tension to the underlying brachialis, which pushes the biceps up to accentuate the peak.

cues.setup: Use a shoulder-width grip on the outer curves of the EZ-bar to reduce wrist strain. For dumbbells, perform both arms simultaneously rather than alternating to maintain constant muscle tension.
cues.execution: Focus on supination by driving through your pinkies as you curl upward. Keep elbows relatively fixed at your sides to prevent shoulder takeover.

cues.setup: Use a shoulder-width grip on the outer curves of the EZ-bar to reduce wrist strain. For dumbbells, perform both arms simultaneously rather than alternating to maintain constant muscle tension.
cues.execution: Focus on supination by driving through your pinkies as you curl upward. Keep elbows relatively fixed at your sides to prevent shoulder takeover.

Perform in reverse order of traditional 21s to match the anabolic stimulus (Short -> Full -> Long): start with 7 reps in the shortened top-half (e.g. seated), 7 full-range-of-motion reps, and finish with 7+ lengthened bottom-half partial reps to failure.

cues.setup: Stand tall holding dumbbells.
cues.execution: Curl the weight up using a neutral hammer grip (stronger position engaging brachialis), then rotate your palms fully upward (supinated) at the top and lower the weight under control during the eccentric phase.

rankings.name: Waiter Curl
rankings.note: F-Tier Hell / Worst of the Worst

rankings.name: Cable Lateral Raise
rankings.note: Side Delt #1 Choice

cues.setup: Set cable pulley at around hand height to achieve maximum tension (90-degree angle between cable and forearm) when the side delt is in its most stretched position. Optionally use wrist cuffs (or hold a lacrosse ball inside the cuff) to take forearm/grip fatigue out of the equation.
cues.execution: Raise the cable out and away from your body under control. Provides smooth, even tension across the entire range of motion.

cues.setup: Hook wrists into cuffs on a dual cable stack, step over one cable, turn around, cross cables behind your back, step forward, and perform raises.
cues.execution: Raises both arms simultaneously for double the time efficiency while maintaining optimal stretched tension on side delts.

rankings.name: Machine Shoulder Press
rankings.note: Front Delt #1 Choice

cues.setup: Choose a machine with comfortable neutral or semi-slanted handles that allows a deep overhead stretch at the bottom.
cues.execution: Offers high stability compared to barbell OHP, allowing you to drive front delts straight to complete failure safely.

cues.setup: Hold a dumbbell in one hand while leaning your torso into a bench, rack, or pole with the non-working arm.
cues.execution: Leaning in shifts the resistance curve, placing significantly higher tension on the side delt at the bottom stretched position compared to standard standing raises.

cues.setup: Lie sideways on an incline bench holding a light dumbbell.
cues.execution: Raises the dumbbell across your body with high stretch-position tension and deep range of motion, providing a massive side-delt pump.

rankings.name: Dumbbell/Cable/Machine Front Raises
rankings.note: Worst of the Worst / Redundant

cues.setup: Sit sideways on a reverse pec deck machine to allow one arm at a time to cross further across your chest.
cues.execution: Sweeping one arm across your chest achieves a much deeper stretch on the rear delts than facing forward. Drive back through the elbow while keeping chest firmly braced.
Perform lying down on a bench to maintain tension on the rear delt at the bottom stretch position (unlike standing dumbbell reverse flies).

cues.setup: Set pulleys high, cross your arms in front of your chest holding the cables directly (without handles). Alternate which arm crosses on top from set to set.
cues.execution: Focus on sweeping the cables out and back rather than yanking them. Provides an enormous range of motion with deep stretch and smooth tension across the rear delts.
Use an underhand grip to bias the rear delts over the upper traps.
Solid for overloading rear delts with heavier weights, though mid-traps will partially take over.
Suffers from zero tension at the bottom and a lack of stretch in the starting position.

cues.setup: Set cable stack to high or mid height, turn away from the cable, and extend arms overhead.
cues.execution: Moving the arms overhead puts the long head of the triceps into a deep stretch under high cable tension. Keep elbows tucked near ears and extend through the forearms under control. Shown in studies to produce ~40% more triceps growth compared to standard pushdowns.

cues.setup: Lie flat on a bench using an EZ-bar to reduce wrist strain. Start the range of motion with your arms angled slightly back behind your head rather than straight up vertical to maintain constant tension at the top.
cues.execution: Arc the bar back behind your head on the eccentric phase to get a deep stretch at the bottom rather than stopping literally at your forehead. Drive forearms back up smoothly.

cues.setup: Attach a straight or EZ-bar to a high pulley. Stand tall and pin elbows to sides.
cues.execution: Provides higher rigid stability and overload potential than a rope. Drive the bar down to full elbow extension to maximize stimulus on the medial and lateral heads.

cues.setup: Set dual cable pulleys around waist height. Cross arms overhead, grabbing the opposite cable, and step forward into the scapular plane (arms angled 30–40° forward).
cues.execution: Extends each arm individually in a very natural, comfortable line of pull while hitting the long head in a deep stretch.

cues.setup: Set cable pulley at chest or waist height. Hold cable directly or with a handle and step back.
cues.execution: Drives the arm back behind the torso, allowing the long head to reach its fully contracted/shortened peak squeeze position. Maintain smooth cable tension throughout.

cues.setup: Lie on a flat bench using a shoulder-width grip on the barbell.
cues.execution: Excellent compound movement for massive progressive overload. Keep elbows tucked closer to your ribcage to heavily bias the lateral and medial heads.

cues.setup: Set feet lower on the platform to maximize knee flexion and knee forward displacement. If the machine bottoms out early, place yoga blocks or pads behind your shoulders/upper back to achieve a full, deep stretch.
cues.execution: Lower under control as deep as hip and knee mobility allow. Keep back flat against the pad and drive up through the entire foot. Eliminates balance limitations to direct maximal tension straight to the quads.

cues.setup: Place bar high on the upper traps. Set stance slightly wider than hip-width with toes turned slightly outward.
cues.execution: Keep chest upright and bend knees deeply to allow the knees to track forward over toes, breaking parallel for maximum quad stretch. Drive straight up through the mid-foot.

cues.setup: Set feet slightly forward of the bar path to maintain an upright torso throughout the descent.
cues.execution: Provides high stability so you can safely push sets directly to absolute muscular failure without fear of losing balance or needing a spotter.

cues.setup: Place rear foot on a bench and take a slightly shorter stance than you would for glute bias to force greater knee extension.
cues.execution: Lower single leg deep into knee flexion until calf meets thigh. Drives intense quad tension and fixes side-to-side muscle imbalances.

cues.setup: Set the backrest reclined back rather than completely upright.
cues.execution: Reclining the seat back places the long rectus femoris head into a deeper stretch at the hip, maximizing growth across all 4 quad heads. Pause briefly at full lockout and control the negative.

cues.setup: Kneel on a padded mat with feet unflattened or flat on the floor.
cues.execution: Maintain a straight line from knees through hips to shoulders. Lean backward smoothly by hinging purely at the knees to place an extreme lengthened stretch on the quads before driving back up.

rankings.name: Bosu Ball Squats
rankings.note: Worst of the Worst

rankings.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curls
rankings.note: Anterior Forearm #1 Choice

cues.execution: Simple, basic, and tried-and-true muscle builder for isolated anterior forearm growth. Curl wrists upward with forearms supported.

rankings.name: Dumbbell Wrist Extensions
rankings.note: Posterior Forearm #1 Choice

cues.execution: Simple and highly effective for building the back (extensors) of the forearm. Extend wrists upward while keeping forearms braced on a bench or knees.

rankings.name: Preacher Hammer Curls
rankings.note: Brachioradialis #1 Choice

cues.setup: Perform hammer curls using a neutral grip on a preacher bench.
cues.execution: Increases torso and upper arm stability while placing higher mechanical tension directly onto the brachioradialis compared to standard standing hammer curls.
Awesome option for building up the back of the forearms. Maintain an overhand (pronated) grip throughout the curl. Note that biceps and brachialis still assist to an extent.
Pinch smooth weight plates between your fingers and thumb to target pinch grip strength and forearms. Easy to progressively overload by extending hold time weekly.

rankings.name: Assisted Lat Pulldown Crunch
rankings.note: Upper Abs / Overall

cues.setup: Sit on a lat pulldown machine (or assisted pull-up setup) where the cable provides a light upward pull.
cues.execution: The upward assistance allows you to control the full eccentric stretch at the top and execute a full spinal crunch without form breakdown. Excellent for beginners to master deep-stretch crunches safely.

rankings.name: Face-Away Kneeling/Standing Cable Crunch
rankings.note: Upper Abs / Overall

cues.setup: Position yourself facing AWAY from the cable stack on a kneeling, standing, or seated lat pulldown station. Adjust the backrest/pad to lock your hips firmly in place.
cues.execution: Facing away creates maximum tension at the top stretch position. Focus on flexing your spine by bringing your ribcage down toward your pelvis into a tight C-shape rather than hinging at the hips.

rankings.name: Face-Away Lat Pulldown Cable Crunch
rankings.note: Upper Abs / Overall

cues.setup: Position yourself facing AWAY from the cable stack on a kneeling, standing, or seated lat pulldown station. Adjust the backrest/pad to lock your hips firmly in place.
cues.execution: Facing away creates maximum tension at the top stretch position. Focus on flexing your spine by bringing your ribcage down toward your pelvis into a tight C-shape rather than hinging at the hips.

rankings.name: Garhammer Raise
rankings.note: Lower Abs Focus

cues.setup: Lie on a flat bench with your hips positioned right off the end edge.
cues.execution: Tuck knees in and lower legs as far down as possible without letting feet touch the floor to achieve a deep stretch under tension. Curl your pelvis upward smoothly without using momentum or swaying your legs.

rankings.name: Reverse Crunch (with AbMat)
rankings.note: Lower Abs Focus

cues.setup: Lie on a flat bench placing an AbMat or rolled towel under your lower back to allow your spine to extend fully for a deep stretch at the bottom.
cues.execution: Keep knees bent at 90 degrees. Focus on pushing your tailbone up and curling your pelvis inward toward your ribcage (forming a C-shape) rather than just pulling knees to chest. Control the eccentric on the way down. Extend legs outward to increase difficulty.

rankings.name: Towel / AbMat Crunch
rankings.note: Upper Abs Focus

rankings.name: Facing-Machine Lat Pulldown Cable Crunch
rankings.note: Upper Abs Focus

rankings.name: Hanging Leg Raise (with Slings / Straps)
rankings.note: Lower Abs Focus

rankings.name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
rankings.note: Lower Abs Focus

cues.setup: Support upper body on forearm pads (Captain's Chair) or hang from straps/bar.
cues.execution: Do not simply lift your legs with your hip flexors. Focus on actively curling your pelvis upward to round the lower spine into a C-shape so the lower abs initiate the pull.

rankings.name: Garhammer Hold
rankings.note: Lower Abs Focus

cues.setup: Hang hips off the end of a bench and tuck knees into chest.
cues.execution: Lower your legs to the point of maximum stretched tension and hold isometrically. High lower-abs activation in the stretched position.

rankings.name: Reverse Crunch (Flat Bench)
rankings.note: Lower Abs Focus

rankings.name: Hanging Leg Raise with C-Shape Curl

cues.setup: Support upper body on forearm pads (Captain's Chair) or hang from straps/bar.
cues.execution: Do not simply lift your legs with your hip flexors. Focus on actively curling your pelvis upward to round the lower spine into a C-shape so the lower abs initiate the pull.

rankings.name: Hanging Straight Leg / Bent Knee Raise
Bosu Ball / Jump Squat style variations

cues.execution: Elevate hands on blocks or handles to allow the chest to drop below hand level for a full lengthened stretch. As you press up, body angle becomes more perpendicular to gravity, creating an optimal lengthened resistance curve.

rankings.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
rankings.note: Low incline, upper chest focus

rankings.name: Dips
rankings.note: For chest

cues.setup: Attach a bar (not a rope) to a cable stack.
cues.execution: Avoid using rope attachments, as spreading ropes wastes energy at lockout and forces load reductions at the crucial bottom stretch. Pause 1–2 seconds in the bottom stretched position.

rankings.name: Barbell Front Raises (Prone Grip / Pinkies Up)

cues.execution: Perform with a pronated grip pointing pinkies slightly upward (rather than thumbs up) to engage side delt fibers. Lower slowly through the eccentric phase under control.

rankings.name: Prime Machine Row (Chest Supported)
rankings.note: God tier

cues.execution: Use chest support to eliminate lower back fatigue during upper/mid-back rowing. Place weight on the top pin to maximize mechanical tension at full stretch.

rankings.name: Dumbbell Pullover
rankings.note: Or cable lat prayer / EZ-bar pullover

cues.execution: Arc the load back over your head to place lats and long head of the triceps under peak stretch tension without fatiguing your forearms/grip.
Start in a deep stretch. As you pull up, leverage your hips up slightly to adjust leverage dynamically, increasing mechanical advantage at lockout while keeping maximum stretch tension at the bottom.

rankings.name: Seated Leg Extension
rankings.note: Standard setup; reclined for a full stretch it's A to S

cues.execution: Recline the backrest backward as far as possible (extending hips from 90° to ~40°) to stretch the rectus femoris and dramatically boost quad growth.
